clue.text: Have a fancy for sole in an extravagant way

parts.note: to have a fancy for something is to want it
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A diner splurges on a fish dish, ordering sole lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' tempts as the fish, but here it is the adjective meaning single.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantonly can mean lavishly or without restraint, matching an extravagant manner.

clue.text: Closely wrapped first of serious injuries

parts.note: wound, from wind, means wrapped tightly round

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Bound up tightly after the first of some grave injuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Wounds are bodily injuries, especially cuts.

clue.text: New type of willow appears comparatively curious

parts.note: the osier is a willow used for basketwork

explanation.surface: A new variety of willow tree appears rather unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosier is the comparative of nosy, meaning more inquisitive.

clue.text: Stay out somewhat longer than intended

definitions.text: Stay out somewhat longer than intended

parts.words: Stay out somewhat longer than intended
parts.note: staying unconscious in bed past the planned waking time

explanation.surface: Lingering away from home later than planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay out' suggests a late night, but it means stay asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversleep is to sleep past the time one meant to wake.

clue.text: Established extended credit, possibly

parts.note: long means extended in length or time
standing, one's reputation, is a kind of credit

explanation.surface: A firm has set up a long period of credit, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-standing describes something that has existed for a long time, established.

clue.text: Someone in cheap lodgings one removed from the file

indicators.note: something removed from a word is taken out of it, so a letter goes

parts.note: a dossier is a file of documents on a subject
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lodger in a flophouse has been struck off the official records.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosser is British slang for a person who sleeps in doss-houses or rough lodgings.

clue.text: Person on horseback having an advantage

definitions.meaning: a horse carrying a rider has ..., one person aboard
being ... is being one ahead of a rival

explanation.surface: A rider in the saddle holds the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: One-up means one point ahead; a horse with one up carries a single rider.

clue.text: Instrument in the kitchen associated with drink

parts.note: to have sided with someone is to have associated with them
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A cook keeps a musical instrument handy next to the booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the kitchen' is orchestral slang for the percussion section.
explanation.definitionFit: A side drum, or snare drum, is a percussion instrument in the orchestra's percussion section.

clue.text: Slip into debt, having become ill again.

indicators.note: into means put inside, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt
a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: Falling back into the red after recovering.
explanation.definitionFit: Relapsed means fallen back into illness after improvement.

clue.text: Blind genius — one somehow missing nothing

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some new way
one missing something has lost it, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A brilliant mind who cannot see is somehow lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes O from ONE, leaving NE; 'somehow' rearranges GENIUS with NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseeing is an adjective meaning sightless, a synonym of blind.

clue.text: Reactionary having prolonged row with a Liberal.

parts.note: a feud is a long-running quarrel

explanation.surface: A diehard conservative has fallen out at length with a Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudal is used loosely to describe outdated, reactionary attitudes harking back to the old order.

clue.text: Dubious stolen vaccine one rejected when recovering

indicators.note: dubious suggests something questionable, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A suspect batch of stolen vaccine was refused by a patient on the mend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one rejected' is a single letter dropped from the fodder before 'Dubious' rearranges what is left; the vaccine story is pure surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Convalescent means getting better after illness, recovering.

clue.text: Legislative assemblies, including Commons

definitions.meaning: formal assemblies, as in the parliaments of Japan or the old Holy Roman Empire
commons are daily rations of food, an allowance like a fixed diet

explanation.surface: Parliaments, with the House of Commons among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commons' looks like the British lower house, but it means food rations; 'including' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are plurals of diet: a parliament and a regular food allowance.

clue.text: Son, filled to the brim, choked .

parts.note: a glass topped up is filled to the brim

explanation.surface: A boy who has eaten until full is left choking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe that is stopped up is choked or blocked.

clue.text: Salesman returned some time before Christmas, by river, perhaps

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word reads the other way

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
Advent is the season leading up to Christmas
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman comes home just before Christmas, maybe by the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Peradventure is an archaic adverb meaning perhaps or by chance.

clue.text: Wants grape juice —- there's no : alternative

parts.note: wants, as in lacks, means needs
must is unfermented grape juice

explanation.surface: A winemaker wanting fresh grape juice has no other option.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs must is an idiom meaning one has no choice in the matter.

clue.text: Counters where a taxi comes up and plies

indicators.note: in a down clue comes up means reads upward, backwards

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
to ply a tool is to use it

explanation.surface: A taxi pulls up and plies its trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Abacuses are counting frames, counters used for arithmetic.

clue.text: Sign crop is no failure

indicators.note: a failure is a collapse, so the letters break up and re-form

explanation.surface: An omen that the harvest hasn't failed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio, the Scorpion, is a sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Pushed, say, by advocate, ate one's words

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: to advocate a cause is to back it
pedalled is pushed with the feet, as a cyclist does, hence say

explanation.surface: Someone pressured by a lawyer ends up retracting their statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpedal is to retract or reverse an earlier position, like eating one's words.

clue.text: Plant in trouble had to be taken over

indicators.note: taken over means turned over, so the run reads backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A gardener's plant was ailing and had to be replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a flowering garden plant from Mexico.

clue.text: Attempt to import rum of poor quality

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a shy is an attempt or throw, as at a coconut shy
rum, in British slang, means strange or odd

explanation.surface: A trader tries bringing in cheap rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink, but it is the adjective for peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy means badly made or of poor quality.

clue.text: Wild dancers spoiled Byron's act

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined or messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A poet's performance was ruined by some unruly dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of Byron's counts as fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Corybantes were the frenzied dancing priests of the goddess Cybele.

clue.text: Celebration, given what's maybe an Oscar part

indicators.note: part of a phrase signals that the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: A party thrown after winning a prize for a film role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar part' suggests a film role, but 'part' says the answer sits inside 'maybe an Oscar'; 'given what's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British slang for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Cut lyrics originally penned by a band

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn round the body

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A songwriter's words were first written by a pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but it is a strip of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Slash means to cut with a sweeping stroke.

clue.text: Turned up for a particular flight

definitions.text: Turned up for a particular flight

parts.words: Turned up for a particular flight
parts.note: a flight of stairs that turns round as it rises, winding upward

explanation.surface: Someone arrived for a specific plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' reads as air travel, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral staircase is a flight that coils upward around a central column.

clue.text: Tricked one into silly duel, following request

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this part is placed behind the request

parts.note: to beg is to request earnestly

indicators.note: into means put inside, so a letter goes within another piece
silly suggests the letters are rearranged foolishly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone was conned into a foolish fight after being asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges DUEL into ULED, and I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beguiled means deceived or charmed into something, synonymous with tricked.

clue.text: Auditor's old office had a detector

indicators.note: an auditor is a hearer, so what follows is as heard

parts.note: the censor held an ancient Roman magistracy, an old office

explanation.surface: An accountant's former office contained a monitoring device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant but means a listener; 'had a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensor is a device that detects light, heat or movement.

clue.text: Such' figures still found to be hard?

definitions.text: Such' figures still found to be hard?

parts.words: Such' figures still found to be hard?
parts.note: motionless figures made of stone or bronze, which are hard to the touch

explanation.surface: Asking whether certain numbers are still proving difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' looks like numbers and 'still' like 'yet', but they mean motionless statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuary means statues collectively, still figures carved in hard materials.
